mechanism_narrative: The continued rebound in WORKPLACES mobility will translate into more weekday shopping trips, pushing RETAIL_REC upward over the next four weeks as commuting-linked errands normalize.
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES rises or stays near current levels but RETAIL_REC remains more negative than in the prior 28 days, the mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp improvement in GROCERY_PHARM indicates easing essential-trip caution; when it crosses above its recent trend, discretionary retail follows within one to two weeks and lifts RETAIL_REC.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises by at least 3 points week-on-week after being above -15 for one week
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM improves through the stated threshold and RETAIL_REC does not improve within two weeks, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT and WORKPLACES rise together, they jointly indicate stronger trip chaining and downtown activity, which increases RETAIL_REC over the following four weeks more than either series alone.
failure_condition: If simultaneous increases in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES are followed by flat or declining RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days, the interaction claim is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Persistent gains in RESIDENTIAL mobility signal more time spent near home and more local spending on necessities, which suppresses discretionary retail visits and keeps RETAIL_REC lower over the next month.
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL stays elevated or rises further while RETAIL_REC improves over the next 28 days, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A renewed drop in PARKS mobility below its recent range captures renewed mobility restraint and lower leisure activity, which should spill over into weaker retail-and-recreation mobility within one week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls below -60 after having been above -60 in the prior week
failure_condition: If PARKS breaks below the stated threshold and RETAIL_REC does not weaken within seven days, the mechanism does not hold.

mechanism_narrative: Improvement in PARKS together with TRANSIT indicates broader restoration of out-of-home movement; this combined signal should raise discretionary retail visits over a two-week horizon.
failure_condition: If PARKS and TRANSIT both improve but RETAIL_REC does not become less negative within two weeks, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM and RESIDENTIAL both remain elevated while WORKPLACES stays weak, the pattern reflects household-based activity concentration that diverts time away from discretionary shopping and depresses RETAIL_REC over four weeks.
failure_condition: If elevated GROCERY_PHARM and RESIDENTIAL coincide with stronger RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days, the mechanism fails.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in TRANSIT from its current depressed level should first lift access to shopping districts and then support retail visits, but only if WORKPLACES does not fall further; otherwise the retail effect will not materialize.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises by at least 3 points week-on-week while WORKPLACES does not decline by more than 1 point
failure_condition: If TRANSIT rebounds under the stated condition but RETAIL_REC fails to improve within two weeks, or WORKPLACES weakens materially and RETAIL_REC still rises, the hypothesis is rejected.
